findings.passage: The comedian Gianmarco Soresi, who worked with her on _Ginger Twinsies_, has interviewed her twice on his podcast
findings.problem: Factual error about a named person. Soresi was not in Ginger Twinsies. Playbill's cast list (Russell Daniels, Aneesa Folds, Jimmy Ray Bennett, Lakisha May, Grace Reiter, Phillip Taratula, Matthew Wilkas, Mitch Wood) omits him. On her show in September 2025 he jokes that more people will see her clip on his podcast "than we'll ever see Ginger Twinsies" (S27 0:07:05), and she says "Me and Russell have broken that one scene ... 'Oh, like Annie, it's you'" (S27 0:41:14). Her castmate was his co-host Russell Daniels (named as co-host in S20 0:00:20; in S39's YouTube description), who played Annie. The research log flagged this credit as an unconfirmed inference to check against a cast list; the article prints it as fact. It is also the phrase meant to fix unfamiliar-03 and unfamiliar-04, so both decisions fail. C64's claim text repeats the error.
findings.acceptance_test: The body no longer says Soresi worked with her on Ginger Twinsies. He is identified by a relationship the record supports (for example, a comedian who has interviewed her twice on his podcast The Downside and was a guest on hers). If the co-host is mentioned, he is named accurately as Russell Daniels, her Ginger Twinsies castmate, with a source. The S39 compliment lines stay attributed to 'one of the two hosts' unless audio assigns them. C64's claim text and the unfamiliar-03/04 resolutions are updated to match.

findings.passage: She never did plays or musicals in school, the Leader-Telegram reported.
findings.problem: The evidence record knows of a conflicting first-person account and the article omits it. In October 2025 (S29 0:31:44-0:32:10) she described playing Elizabeth Proctor in a high-school production of The Crucible and having a coughing attack on stage. In April 2026 (S44 0:07:03-0:07:10) she agreed she did no plays because she was "too afraid". The standard asks that disputed claims be attributed and given the relevant response.
findings.acceptance_test: Either the sentence notes the conflict in one clause (for example, that she has also described playing Elizabeth Proctor in a high-school Crucible), or it is cut and the live-record sentence rests on Stapleview and Ginger Twinsies. C123's text matches.

findings.passage: That was to [Page Six](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LB8IV4nRnX0) in December 2025. Of the parody she said, "If I don't get a million, I'm actually going to be really really embarrassed."
findings.problem: The second quote comes from I Never Liked You (S46, August 2026) but carries no source or date and sits right after a Page Six attribution, so a reader will assign it to Page Six in December 2025.
findings.acceptance_test: The million-views quote names its conversation and date (I Never Liked You, August 2026), or is linked at the quote.

findings.passage: First, she asks permission more than she polishes an image. A Three, even a modest one, tends to claim the role and manage how it looks. Reiter asks whether she is allowed: "Is that okay?" on her own overshare show
findings.problem: The leading exhibit admits the rival reading. Asking "Is that okay?" about what she has just disclosed on a public podcast can be image monitoring, which is what the paragraph assigns to the Three. The paragraph's stronger exhibits are her 2022 "allowing myself to say I'm a comedian" and the Michos' testimony that she walks a question back when not answered at once, but the paragraph never tests the image reading of its lead example.
findings.acceptance_test: The discriminator paragraph either leads with the exhibits that are about permission rather than disclosure (the 2022 'allowing myself' line, 'Do you want me to only if you want me to?', the walk-it-down testimony), or adds one clause conceding that 'Is that okay?' could also be image-checking and saying why the pattern still leans Six.
